why: The 321 tracked Python lines here are three unrelated jobs wearing one directory name, and they do not get the same answer. mutate_launcher_check.py earns keep-ours on a property nothing off-the-shelf has: it mutates a PowerShell file, and no maintained mutation tester mutates PowerShell -- Stryker ships JS/TS, C# and Scala mutators only, mutmut and cosmic-ray walk the Python AST, and universalmutator's published rule set (universal.rules + c_like.rules + a per-language file for Python/Swift/Solidity/C/C++/Java) names no PowerShell file; on top of that it restores the operator's LIVE launcher by byte copy and proves the restore with sha256 (mutate_launcher_check.py:80-88), because a text-mode round trip silently rewrote that LF file with CRLF, a 184-byte diff a reviewer would not see. Verified this session: both mutations CAUGHT, exit 0, 'launcher restored, sha256 unchanged 7661ee27e42d', git status clean. make_lane_launchers.py does NOT earn it, and I will not pretend otherwise: Ansible's community.windows.win_shortcut sets src/dest/arguments/directory/icon/description/hotkey/windowstyle AND run_as_admin, declares supports_check_mode = $true (the plan/--apply split make_lane_launchers.py hand-rolls), and updates the existing .lnk in place rather than delete-and-recreate -- which is the one property repoint_taskbar_pin.ps1 exists to protect, since recreating a pinned .lnk orphans the pin. Its run_as_admin toggles ShellLinkFlags::RunAsUser (0x2000) through [Ansible.Shortcut.ShellLink]::SetFlags, the SAME bit repoint_taskbar_pin.ps1:52-59 stamps by hand as byte 21 mask 0x20 (byte 21 is the second byte of the little-endian LinkFlags DWORD, so 0x20 << 8 = 0x2000). The only thing standing between that module and adoption is that Ansible cannot run its control node on Windows at all -- documented, not a preference -- so buying it costs a WSL install that Ansible's own docs decline to support. log_session_lesson.py is not a build-vs-buy question, it is a spent one-off: it hardcodes ONE row as a module constant (log_session_lesson.py:20-55) and 89 lines now produce the output 'L-2026-07-27-c already present; nothing to do', verified by running it. It belongs with the eight untracked dated scripts sitting beside it, under the same reason out-of-scope.txt already uses for work-docs/audits, or behind a generic 10-line append-a-lesson CLI -- not defended as tooling.

alternatives.name: Ansible community.windows.win_shortcut (docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/community/windows/win_shortcut_module.html)
alternatives.covers: Everything make_lane_launchers.py does and most of repoint_taskbar_pin.ps1: creates/updates a .lnk from src/dest/arguments/directory/icon/description/hotkey/windowstyle, idempotently. Two properties this repo hand-built are already in it: supports_check_mode = $true in the module spec, which is the plan-then---apply split make_lane_launchers.py:110-112 writes itself; and it builds 'an in-memory object based on the existing shortcut (if any)' then calls $ShortCut.Save(), i.e. modifies in place instead of delete/recreate, which is exactly what keeps a taskbar pin alive. run_as_admin flips ShellLinkFlags::RunAsUser (0x2000) via [Ansible.Shortcut.ShellLink]::SetFlags -- the same bit repoint_taskbar_pin.ps1:52-59 reads and re-stamps as byte 21 mask 0x20.
alternatives.gap: Ansible cannot run its control node on Windows -- 'Ansible cannot run on Windows as the control node due to API limitations on the platform' (Managing Windows hosts guide); the workaround is a WSL distro, and the same docs say WSL 'is not supported by Ansible and should not be used for production systems'. So adopting it on a Windows-native, pwsh-and-stdlib-Python harness means installing WSL plus a Windows connection plugin to configure the machine the control node is already sitting on. Beyond that: no .bak plus -Revert pair (repoint_taskbar_pin.ps1:63-68, 91), no post-write read-back verification of the written arguments AND the elevation bit (repoint_taskbar_pin.ps1:106-115), and nothing that tells you the pinned .lnk is the only launcher the operator actually clicks -- which is the whole defect L-2026-07-27-c records.
alternatives.cost: ansible-core + the community.windows collection + a WSL distro + a Windows connection transport (WinRM/SSH), on a repo whose current cost for this job is 139 lines of stdlib Python shelling out to powershell.exe. Free/OSS (GPLv3 for ansible-core).
alternatives.maturity: Verified this session by reading the module documentation page and the current main-branch plugins/modules/win_shortcut.ps1 source on GitHub. NOT verified: release cadence of the collection, whether run_as_admin survives a Save() round trip in practice the way the hand-rolled byte stamp is asserted to, and whether the module preserves an existing IconLocation when icon is omitted.

alternatives.name: WinGet Configuration / Microsoft DSC 3.0 (learn.microsoft.com/windows/package-manager/configuration)
alternatives.covers: The Windows-native declarative-desired-state answer: a YAML file describing the machine, applied idempotently with `winget configure`, plus export of the current device's configuration. It is the first-party version of the plan/apply idiom every script in this directory reimplements by hand, and unlike Ansible it runs natively on the machine it configures.
alternatives.gap: I found no first-party DSC resource for .lnk shortcuts and none for taskbar pins in the WinGet Configuration docs or the microsoft/winget-dsc samples -- the shipped samples are package installs and OS/app settings. Shortcut and pin work would land in a Script resource wrapping the same WScript.Shell + byte-21 code that exists here now, so adoption would move the code, not delete it. Covers nothing at all of the other two jobs (PowerShell mutation testing, the lessons ledger).
alternatives.cost: Effectively zero install weight -- winget and DSC 3.0 ship with current Windows. That is the strongest thing about this option and the reason it deserves the recheck below.
alternatives.maturity: Actively developed by Microsoft; DSC 3.0 and the `dscv3` command documented as current in 2026 sources. NOT verified: I searched Microsoft's docs and the winget-dsc samples directory, not the PowerShell Gallery, so I cannot claim no community shortcut resource exists.

alternatives.name: chezmoi (chezmoi.io)
alternatives.covers: A cross-platform (including Windows) machine-state manager built on exactly this directory's idiom: `chezmoi diff` then `chezmoi apply`, with templating and run_once_ scripts. It would hold Start-Claude.ps1 and the four-lane table (Start-Claude.ps1:38-47, duplicated at make_lane_launchers.py:45-54 -- a real duplication chezmoi would collapse) as one templated source of truth across machines.
alternatives.gap: chezmoi manages file CONTENT under a target tree. A .lnk is an opaque binary whose properties -- arguments, icon index, the RunAsUser flag -- chezmoi has no model of, and the pinned shortcut lives in %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\Quick Launch\User Pinned\TaskBar, not a dotfile tree. Storing the pin as a blob and copying it over would preserve the elevation bit but overwrite whatever icon the operator set on that machine, which repoint_taskbar_pin.ps1:92,101 deliberately reads and carries forward.
alternatives.cost: Single Go binary, free/OSS, Windows-friendly. Low.
alternatives.maturity: Widely used dotfile manager. NOT VERIFIED this session: I did not fetch chezmoi's documentation, so the shortcut-handling gap above is reasoning from what chezmoi is, not from a doc page I read. Current release cadence also not verified.

alternatives.name: Windows Terminal JSON fragment extensions (learn.microsoft.com/windows/terminal/json-fragment-extensions)
alternatives.covers: The cheapest real replacement for make_lane_launchers.py: one JSON file dropped in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows Terminal\Fragments\ declaring a profiles array, one entry per lane, each with name, startingDirectory and commandline. That is the four desktop shortcuts, with no Python, no COM, no .lnk file format, and the entries appear in the Terminal dropdown. First-party since WT 1.7.
alternatives.gap: A fragment profile sets a commandline, not an environment variable, so CLAUDE_LANE still has to be smuggled into the command string exactly as make_lane_launchers.py:63 does today. Fragments cannot touch the taskbar pin, and the pin is the entire surface where the 11-hour defect lived (the chooser and the desktop shortcuts both existed and worked while every real session still opened through the old pin). No plan/apply diff and no missing-directory guard (make_lane_launchers.py:120-122).
alternatives.cost: Zero. One JSON file, first-party, Windows Terminal already installed at ~/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WindowsApps/wt.exe per make_lane_launchers.py:42.
alternatives.maturity: Documented Microsoft feature, current 2026 Learn page. NOT verified: whether a fragment-declared profile can be pinned to the taskbar as its own pin, which is what would make this a full replacement rather than a partial one.

alternatives.name: mise (mise.jdx.dev) and direnv (direnv.net)
alternatives.covers: The general form of 'export CLAUDE_LANE before starting claude': a per-directory config that sets environment variables on entering the directory, with no launcher, no shortcut and no COM involved.
alternatives.gap: This is the DEFECT, not the fix, and the repo has an executable oracle saying so. Both tools derive the environment FROM the directory; tests/test_workspace_launcher.py:107-127 asserts a path is never read back as a lane, and it is not a style preference -- lanes A and B both resolve to ~/claude-setup (Start-Claude.ps1:39-42), so a directory cannot determine the lane even in principle. Platform gap on top: direnv has no native PowerShell support (issue #1274 documents it emitting malformed PowerShell and upcasing variables it should not touch); mise has added PowerShell support but users report breakage on Windows PowerShell 5.1 requiring PowerShell 7.
alternatives.maturity: Both actively maintained; mise's PowerShell support confirmed present via its own GitHub discussion #6733. NOT verified: current mise release, or whether the 5.1 breakage is resolved.

alternatives.name: Stryker Mutator (stryker-mutator.io), mutmut, cosmic-ray
alternatives.covers: The mutation-testing shelf: automatic mutant generation plus a killed/survived report against an existing suite -- the general form of what mutate_launcher_check.py does for two specific mutants.
alternatives.gap: None of them can read the target. Stryker ships JavaScript/TypeScript, C# and Scala mutators (its own site and 2026 third-party guides); the mutation target here is Start-Claude.ps1, a .ps1. mutmut and cosmic-ray mutate the Python AST and cannot touch a PowerShell file either. Separately, none of them restores the mutated file by byte copy and proves the restore with a sha256 comparison (mutate_launcher_check.py:80-88) -- which matters here because the mutated file is the operator's live taskbar launcher, not a build artifact -- and none preserves LF endings through the round trip, the exact bug that docstring records.
alternatives.cost: Free/OSS, but Stryker.NET means a .NET toolchain and StrykerJS a Node one, for a tool that cannot parse the language in question.
alternatives.maturity: Stryker actively maintained per its own site and 2026 guides; mutmut and cosmic-ray both actively maintained per this repo's own tools-audit-mutations.json record. NOT verified: that no PowerShell mutation plugin exists anywhere unindexed -- I searched and found none, which is weaker than proving absence.

alternatives.name: universalmutator (github.com/agroce/universalmutator)
alternatives.covers: Structurally the closest published match to mutate_launcher_check.py: regex-rule mutation with no parser at all, and an arbitrary shell command as the kill oracle -- the same model as 'rewrite two lines of the .ps1, then run one named pytest node'. Pure Python, no dependencies beyond the stdlib, which matches this repo's dependency habit exactly.
alternatives.gap: Its rules are per-language files (universal.rules + c_like.rules + e.g. swift.rules); the published language list in the README, the ICSE 2018 demo paper and the 2024 ACM paper names Python, Swift, Solidity, C/C++ and Java, not PowerShell -- so PowerShell rules are hand-authored work, in a second rule DSL. And its mutants are generic operator/constant rewrites, whereas both mutations here are the ACTUAL historical defects (lane inferred from -Path; a silent lane-C default), which no generic rule generates and which are the only mutants worth running.
alternatives.maturity: Academic tool with an ICSE 2018 demo and a 2024 ACM paper; a Trail of Bits blog post dated 2026-04-01 on mutation testing is in the result set. NOT VERIFIED: I read search results, the README summary and paper abstracts, NOT the repo's rules/ directory, so I cannot state there is no powershell.rules file -- only that no source I found names one. Current maintenance cadence also not verified.

alternatives.name: adr-tools (adr.github.io/adr-tooling) and log4brains (github.com/thomvaill/log4brains)
alternatives.covers: The job log_session_lesson.py is doing: appending an immutable, identified, supersedes-linked decision record. log4brains' model -- 'an ADR is immutable, only its status can change... it can be deprecated or superseded by another one' -- is exactly the shape of the row at log_session_lesson.py:20-55 (id, ts, status closed, supersedes_context L-2026-07-27-a, lesson, why_it_happened, fix, residual). `log4brains adr new` is the CLI this script is a single hardcoded instance of.
alternatives.gap: Both write one markdown file per record, not JSONL rows into state/lessons.jsonl (25 rows, verified), which is the format the harness reads; log4brains additionally drags in Node and a static-site publisher this repo has no use for. But the honest gap points the other way: log_session_lesson.py implements no ledger API at all. It hardcodes ONE row as a module constant, so its 89 lines emit a single JSON line and are inert afterwards -- running it this session printed 'L-2026-07-27-c already present; nothing to do'. Neither ADR tool nor this script is the right comparison; the right comparison is a ~10-line generic `append-lesson --id --lesson` CLI, which the repo does not have.
alternatives.cost: adr-tools is bash scripts, needing Git Bash on Windows; log4brains is an npm/Node global install. Both free/OSS.
alternatives.maturity: adr-tools is the long-established reference implementation of the Nygard format; log4brains is published on npm and used by AWS ParallelCluster UI and Lullabot per their public ADR sites. NOT verified: recent commit activity for either project.

evidence: READ IN FULL: tools/workspace/make_lane_launchers.py:1-139, tools/workspace/log_session_lesson.py:1-89, tools/workspace/mutate_launcher_check.py:1-93 (these three are the 321 Python lines this record scopes), plus the two PowerShell files in the same directory as context because they are what the Python acts on -- tools/workspace/Start-Claude.ps1:1-184 (the mutation target and the lane chooser) and tools/workspace/repoint_taskbar_pin.ps1:1-115 -- and tests/test_workspace_launcher.py:1-160, the oracle both mutations aim at. Also read docs/prior-art/tools-gate.json in full and the first ~4000 bytes of docs/prior-art/tools-audit-mutations.json for calibration, docs/prior-art/out-of-scope.txt in full, docs/CODEBASE-MAP.md:414, and the first 14 lines of each of the 8 UNTRACKED one-off scripts in this directory (add_license.py, clean_oren_roast.py, fix_false_claims.py, fix_power_transform_readme.py, polish_memes_readme.py, repo_activity.py, repo_activity_days.py, ship_claude_memes.py, 964 lines total, outside our_loc). COMMANDS RUN: `git ls-files tools/workspace/ | xargs wc -l` (321 tracked Python lines across 3 files, 299 PowerShell lines across 2); `grep -rn CLAUDE_LANE` across the repo and ~/.claude/hooks -- the ONLY consumer of the variable every launcher here exists to set is ~/.claude/hooks/session-recall.sh:43,52,59, which lives OUTSIDE this repo, so the contract is unversioned relative to its producers; `python tools/workspace/log_session_lesson.py` (plan mode, printed 'L-2026-07-27-c already present; nothing to do', proving it is spent); `python tools/workspace/mutate_launcher_check.py` (both mutations CAUGHT, exit 0, 'launcher restored, sha256 unchanged 7661ee27e42d', git status clean afterwards); `wc -l state/lessons.jsonl` (25 rows). SEARCHES: 8 WebSearch queries -- Ansible win_shortcut check_mode; Ansible control node on Windows/WSL; PowerShell mutation testing / Pester / Stryker; universalmutator supported languages; chezmoi vs WinGet Configuration DSC for Windows workstation setup; Windows Terminal JSON fragment extensions; direnv/mise PowerShell support on Windows; adr-tools/log4brains decision-record CLIs; Windows 11 programmatic taskbar pin/unpin (corroborates repoint_taskbar_pin.ps1:16-17 -- the Shell.Application taskbarpin verb can unpin but no longer pin on Windows 11). 2 WebFetch: the win_shortcut docs page, and the raw main-branch plugins/modules/win_shortcut.ps1 source. NOT VERIFIED, plainly: I installed and ran nothing third-party -- no Ansible, no WinGet DSC, no chezmoi, no universalmutator -- so every claim about what those tools would do here comes from their documentation and source, not from a run against a real .lnk on this machine. I did not read universalmutator's rules/ directory. I did not search the PowerShell Gallery for a community DSC shortcut resource. I did not fetch chezmoi's docs. I did not verify that byte 21 mask 0x20 and ShellLinkFlags::RunAsUser 0x2000 are the same bit by inspecting an actual .lnk -- that equivalence is arithmetic on the little-endian LinkFlags DWORD, not a measurement.
recheck: Run all four, in order. (1) `python C:/Users/shova/claude-setup/tools/workspace/mutate_launcher_check.py` -- must print CAUGHT twice, 'launcher restored, sha256 unchanged', and exit 0; if it prints SURVIVED or 'anchor text not found, mutation is stale', the keep-ours half of this verdict is dead and the file is decoration. (2) `python C:/Users/shova/claude-setup/tools/workspace/log_session_lesson.py` -- if it still prints 'already present; nothing to do', the split's second half is still true and those 89 lines are still inert; that is the trigger to move it to docs/prior-art/out-of-scope.txt under the work-docs/audits reason or replace it with a generic append-lesson CLI. (3) `git -C C:/Users/shova/claude-setup log --oneline -1 -- tools/workspace/make_lane_launchers.py` and `grep -rn 'make_lane_launchers' C:/Users/shova/claude-setup --include=*.md --include=*.ps1 --include=*.py` -- if nothing references it and the taskbar pin plus Start-Claude.ps1 are the only live path, the answer for that file is delete, not buy. (4) WebSearch "Stryker PowerShell mutator" and "universalmutator powershell.rules", then `gh api repos/agroce/universalmutator/contents/universalmutator/static --jq '.[].name'` to list the shipped rule files -- if a PowerShell rule set or a PowerShell Stryker plugin now exists, re-open the keep-ours half. Separately, `winget configure --help` and a PowerShell Gallery search for a DSC shortcut resource -- if a first-party or well-maintained DSC resource can write a .lnk with run_as_admin in place, the Windows-native adopt path opens without the WSL tax that currently rules Ansible out.
what_ours_does: Three unrelated jobs, one directory. (1) make_lane_launchers.py:1-139 generates four Windows .lnk desktop shortcuts, one per charter lane, by formatting a WScript.Shell PowerShell template (make_lane_launchers.py:76-86) and shelling out to powershell.exe (make_lane_launchers.py:127-129). Each shortcut runs wt.exe -d <lane dir> pwsh -NoExit -Command "$env:CLAUDE_LANE='<lane>'; claude" (make_lane_launchers.py:63,69), so the lane is DECLARED in the environment instead of inferred from a working directory. It defaults to plan-only and needs --apply to write (make_lane_launchers.py:110-112), skips lanes whose directory is missing (make_lane_launchers.py:120-122), and returns nonzero if any shortcut fails. The lane table (make_lane_launchers.py:45-54) duplicates the one in Start-Claude.ps1:38-47. (2) mutate_launcher_check.py:1-93 is mutation testing for a PowerShell file: it reintroduces the two ACTUAL historical defects into Start-Claude.ps1 -- inferring a lane from -Path, and silently defaulting a no-argument run to lane C (mutate_launcher_check.py:30-45) -- and asserts the matching pytest node in tests/test_workspace_launcher.py fails for each. All I/O is binary on purpose (mutate_launcher_check.py:69-76) because a text-mode rewrite turned that LF file into CRLF, a silent 184-byte diff; the original is restored in a finally block and the restore is PROVED by sha256 comparison, with the .mutbak copy kept if the hashes differ (mutate_launcher_check.py:80-88). (3) log_session_lesson.py:1-89 appends exactly one hardcoded JSON row (log_session_lesson.py:20-55, lesson L-2026-07-27-c) to state/lessons.jsonl, skipping if the id is already present, writing in binary append mode with an explicit b'\n' so Windows text mode cannot put a CRLF terminator on one row out of 25 (log_session_lesson.py:76-79), then re-reading the file to verify the row landed. NOT COUNTED in our_loc but living in the same directory and inseparable from what the Python means: Start-Claude.ps1:1-184, the chooser the taskbar pin now opens (global lane / existing repo / scaffold-a-new-repo, with -Path deliberately never resolving a lane at Start-Claude.ps1:112-114), and repoint_taskbar_pin.ps1:1-115, which rewrites the pinned .lnk IN PLACE -- never renaming it, because renaming a pinned .lnk orphans the pin -- carrying the icon (repoint_taskbar_pin.ps1:92,101) and re-stamping the run-as-administrator bit at header byte 21 flag 0x20 that WScript.Shell's Save() clears (repoint_taskbar_pin.ps1:52-59,104), with a .bak, a -Revert, and a read-back verification of both properties before exiting 0. Also uncounted: 8 untracked dated one-off remediation scripts (964 lines) that are the same species as log_session_lesson.py.
strongest_counterargument: Calling this 'split' overstates how much of it is worth keeping, and the record buries the sharper finding under a build-vs-buy frame. Of 321 lines, exactly 93 -- mutate_launcher_check.py -- survive on merit, and even those pass a test suite that only exists because the launcher is a hand-rolled PowerShell script in the first place; adopt Windows Terminal fragment profiles and the launcher, its test file, and its mutation harness all disappear together, taking the 'no PowerShell mutator exists' argument with them, because there would be no PowerShell to mutate. That is not a keep-ours property, it is a cost this repo chose and is now defending. Meanwhile make_lane_launchers.py is very likely already dead: nothing outside the file and this record references it, the desktop shortcuts it writes are precisely the artifact L-2026-07-27-c calls 'installed next to the habit instead of inside it', and the taskbar pin now opens the chooser instead -- so its real verdict is delete, which is not one of the four words this schema offers, and 'split' quietly absorbs it. And the whole design rests on a contract that nothing in this repo tests: CLAUDE_LANE's only consumer is ~/.claude/hooks/session-recall.sh, a file outside version control here, so the launcher could keep exporting a variable the hook stopped reading and every check in tests/test_workspace_launcher.py would still be green. A harsher reviewer would file this component as one 93-line keeper, one dead file, one spent one-off, and an untested cross-repo contract -- and would be right.
